newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel says dilution limited by longer license.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel says dilution limited by longer license.

text.p: Eurotunnel executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle said in a French newspaper interview that the decision by the French and British to study an extension the Channel Tunnel operator's licence would limit the dilution of shareholders' equity in a debt restructuring.

"(The extension) would give our shareholders an additional opportunity to limit the dilution -- the plan envisages the distribution of free warrants exerciseable to 2001," he told the weekly Journal des Finances.
A copy of the interview was sent to Reuters.
Ponsolle reiterated that Eurotunnel was ahead of targets for the first half "which augurs well for 1997 and coming years."

He said Le Shuttle tourist activity since the start of 1997 has been good. "We have kept 35 to 40 percent of the market share despite being able to offer two hourly departures, or half of our previous capacity," he was quoted as saying.

He said repairs to a fire-damaged section of the subsea tunnel cost 350 million francs, compared with estimates of 300 to 500 million. The cost was covered by insurance, as well as operating losses, he said. It will pay only five percent of the 1.8 billion franc cost of the accident.
Insurance premiums have risen by 20 percent but have clauses allowing downward revisions if there are no accidents in the next few years, he said.
Daily traffic since the resumption of the Le Shuttle freight service on June 15 averaged more than 1,000 lorries, he said.
